    - article:
      - heading "TOTAL PROBABILITY THEOREM" [level=2]
      - paragraph: "If {A₁, A₂, …, Aₙ} is a complete partition of S, then for any event B:"
      - paragraph: P(B) = ∑ᵢ P(Aᵢ) P(B | Aᵢ)
      - heading "Partition conditions" [level=3]
      - paragraph:
        - text: M₁ ∪ M₂ = S (collectively exhaustive)
        - img
      - paragraph:
        - text: M₁ ∩ M₂ = ∅ (mutually exclusive)
        - img
      - paragraph: "Here, B = D (defective items) and the partition is {M₁, M₂}."
      - text: For positive-probability partition events. A zero-weight source contributes zero; its supplied defect rate is a model parameter, not a conditional ratio on an observed event.
    - article:
      - heading "WHY THE THEOREM WORKS (4-STEP DERIVATION)" [level=2]
      - list:
        - listitem: "Since {Aᵢ} is a partition, B = ⋃ᵢ (B ∩ Aᵢ), a disjoint union."
        - listitem: The events B ∩ Aᵢ are mutually exclusive.
        - listitem: Therefore P(B) = ∑ᵢ P(B ∩ Aᵢ).
        - listitem: By conditional probability, P(B ∩ Aᵢ) = P(Aᵢ)P(B | Aᵢ).
      - paragraph: Thus P(B) = ∑ᵢ P(Aᵢ)P(B | Aᵢ).
    - article:
      - heading "WORKED EXAMPLE (Factory scenario)" [level=2]
      - paragraph: "A factory’s items come from two machines:"
      - paragraph: P(M₁) = 0.60, P(D | M₁) = 0.02 P(M₂) = 0.40, P(D | M₂) = 0.05
      - paragraph: Find P(D).
      - paragraph: P(D) = 0.60 × 0.02 + 0.40 × 0.05 = 0.012 + 0.020 = 0.032 = 3.2%
      - paragraph: On average, 3.2 out of every 100 items are defective.
    - article:
      - heading "COMMON MISTAKE" [level=2]:
        - img
        - text: COMMON MISTAKE
      - paragraph: "Do not add raw conditional rates:"
      - paragraph: P(D | M₁) + P(D | M₂) = 2% + 5% = 7% ×
      - paragraph: These rates apply to different groups. Total probability requires weighting by how often each source occurs.
      - text: "Correct approach:"
      - paragraph: P(D) = ∑ P(source) × P(D | source)
